Alex / Team — quick technical answers ahead of Thursday's session.

1) SDK + auth:
- Recommended for POC: Redwood SDK with API keys scoped to environment + short TTL tokens (1 hour) minted by your Okta OIDC flow. For prod: use mTLS for private deployments or short-lived JWTs via our token-exchange endpoint (we emit audit_event when a token is minted). Sample code: we will include an Okta exchange snippet.

2) Routing & model variants:
- Use request attributes to tag latency vs cost preference. Our router supports policy rules: route to "low-latency" pool (fp16 Llama-optimized / compiled kernels) or "cost-efficient" pool (4-bit quantized variant) with fallback. We'll provide policy YAML in the brief.

3) Structured output & tool-calling:
- Validate post-decode using our JSON schema verifier. If verifier fails, we surface a 2xx with parse_error field in metadata and optionally call a canonical fallback tool that asks the model for a corrected payload (2nd chance).
- For tool invocation reliability: implement idempotent tool calls with a correlation id. Redwood can attach a per-request retry-policy header. If downstream times out, we recommend: return a partial result to client + enqueue async retry, or return a "tool_timeout" structured response so the caller can surface a safe UI state.

4) Embeddings & reranker:
- For retrieval+rerank: default embed dim 1536 is a good balance; if you need semantic nuance (legal language) consider 3072. Re-embedding with a stronger model improves recall at cost. Strong pattern: use cached embeddings + periodic re-embed batch job.

5) Chat vs completions, tokenization, and streaming:
- Chat (stateful): optimized for multi-turn context; system/user/assistant roles preserved. Streaming in chat streams deltas that may include chunked tool-call signals. Good for interactive widgets.
- Completions (stateless): simpler single prompt -> completion flow; cheaper when you do independent scoring or reranking of candidates.
- Tokenization: token counts depend on tokenizer (we provide tokenizers in SDK). Historical conversational tokens count toward context_limit. We recommend truncating older messages using a sliding window + salient summary.
- max_tokens behavior: it caps generated tokens; ensure you account for decoder/mu tokens and any tool-call payload added after generation.
- stop sequences: supported for both APIs; streaming will still emit partial chunks until model hits stop — our client exposes an onStop callback.
- Streaming semantics: streams commit deltas; finalization events include canonical_output and schema_verifier result. If you need deterministic behavior for tool-calls, use synchronous blocking calls (slightly higher latency) or require an explicit finalization token from the stream before invoking external systems.

I'll bring a short test harness that simulates 200 reqs/s with a 250ms target p50 so we can validate router policies.
